Subject: Tenancy & GPU sizing for MedAcuity POC — decision needed

Hi Sara — great to meet on Friday. Following up with the sizing and tenancy options we discussed for the POC. Attached is a short matrix that lays out three paths: (A) Hosted Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated GPU pools), (B) Private Control Plane + Dedicated GPUs (customer VPC for inference), and (C) On-prem/private appliance.

Quick ask: can you confirm which constraint is a hard requirement for the POC? Options below, pick all that apply and mark priority:
- Data residency in MedAcuity VPC (yes/no)
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM (required/optional)
- Full isolation of model weights from shared storage (yes/no)

On the sizing side, the POC usage estimate you shared (100 concurrent sessions at ~6 tokens/sec average, peak 200 sessions for short bursts) maps to roughly 8x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state with burst capacity up to 12 GPUs using our batching/KV cache profile (we can show the math in the attached PDF). If VPC isolation is required, the minimum starting commitment is 6 GPUs due to scheduling overheads for isolated fleets.

I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi to map the commercial/commit ask. If you can confirm the three constraints above by Wednesday we'll lock in the recommended path and pricing for the POC.

Thanks,

Team — forwarding Sara's answers (below). They require VPC residency and customer-managed KMS for the POC. Core asks for our review:
- Minimum committed footprint to meet 95th pct latency 250ms for short prompts (100 concurrent typical, 200 peak)
- Bump plan for burst windows and commercial ask for an initial POC commitment

I sketched a recommendation in the attached spreadsheet: a hybrid-start approach where we provision 6 dedicated GPUs in their VPC (private control plane) with an option to burst to 10 via reserved capacity in our dedicated pools for the first 90 days. After the POC, we convert to either fully private (on-prem or customer-owned infra) or a dedicated-only footprint based on their production traffic.

Key tradeoffs I point out in the doc:
- Isolation vs unit-cost: full private on-prem has highest isolation but also highest upfront procurement and ops overhead.
- Scheduling efficiency: dedicated shared racks give better GPU utilization; isolated VPC fleets have ~15-25% overhead in throughput per GPU because of smaller packing windows.
- SLA & credits: Dedicated (Redwood-managed) can offer tighter SLA and credits during regional outages; Private requires different SLA wording.

Please review the attachment and drop your comments inline. I flagged the price and minimum-commit numbers for legal.

—Chloe

Chloe / team — reviewed the numbers. A couple of concrete points from infra/commercial:

Sizing math (short):
- Baseline model: 7B parameter quantized to int8, median prompt length 120 tokens.
- Observed throughput: ~6 tokens/sec per session with continuous batching and prefix cache.
- 100 steady concurrent sessions -> ~600 tokens/sec = ~36k tokens/min -> steady-state compute equivalent ~8x A100-80GB for 95th pct latency target.
- Isolation overhead: expect ~18% throughput hit when running in isolated VPC tenant with constrained packing. That pushes effective need to ~9.5 GPUs -> round to 10 GPUs to keep headroom for variance.

Commercial recommendation for POC:
- Commit: 6 GPUs deployed into MedAcuity VPC (private control plane). This satisfies baseline and keeps procurement low.
- Burst: Allow up to +4 GPUs from Redwood Dedicated pool for predictable peak spikes (doc shows cost for 30-day burst usage).
- Conversion trigger: if 30-day rolling average concurrency > 120, convert to 10 GPU committed private fleet or discuss on-prem acquisition.

Notes: if Sara's team insists on model-weights-at-rest isolation, we should include encrypted local volumes and attestations. That adds ~10-12% to infra cost for snapshot and transfer workflows.

I'll prepare a short commercial blurb for Marissa to send with pricing.

-Rishi

Sara / team — thanks for the clarity. Per Rishi's sizing and our internal commercial review, here's the proposal we'll put in the SOW:

Proposal (POC, 90 days):
- Architecture: Private control plane within MedAcuity VPC + customer-owned KMS. Redwood will deploy and manage inference fleet within their VPC (network peering + private endpoints).
- Commit: 6x A100-80GB equiv (dedicated to MedAcuity) + monitoring and tracing.
- Burst: Up to 4x A100-80GB equiv from Redwood Dedicated pool on predefined schedule/alerts. Bursts billed at pre-agreed uplift rate.
- Security add-ons: encrypted local volumes for model weights, periodic audit attestation (monthly) — included in POC price.
- Conversion path: if 30-day rolling average concurrency > 120 or sustained latency drift, convert to 10x GPUs committed within their VPC or discuss on-prem procurement (we'll provide vendor SKU list).
- Pricing: see attached one-pager (high-level). We propose a mitigated discount for POC with conversion credits applied to the committed purchase if they convert within 6 months.

Next steps: Chloe, please send Sara the SOW draft and the DocuSign link (I've attached reviewer comments in the shared drive). Sara — if the proposal looks good we'll need a procurement contact to start EOAs and a PE for networking setup.
